section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the implications of the 'be-creative effect' for divergent thinking, highlighting the top-down nature of creative thought. The present study (referred to as 'Our study') found a 'Matthew effect' where high fluid intelligence amplified the gains in creativity when participants were instructed to 'be creative'. The findings suggest the involvement of executive processes and challenge classic associative models of creativity, proposing future research to investigate strategy use and neural correlates.
